function.arguments:
{"path": "plot_llm_metrics.py", "content": "import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('llm_metrics.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

models = [m['name'] for m in data['models']]
speeds = [m['speed_tokens_per_second'] for m in data['models']]
memories = [m['memory_gb'] for m in data['models']]

# Set up the figure with two subplots side by side
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Bar positions
x = np.arange(len(models))
width = 0.35

# Plot speed (tokens/second)
bars1 = ax1.bar(x - width/2, speeds, width, label='Speed (tokens/sec)', color='#2E86AB')
ax1.set_ylabel('Tokens/Second', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_title('Inference Speed', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=15, ha='right')
ax1.legend()
ax1.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars1:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax1.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height,
             f'{int(height)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

# Plot memory (GB)
bars2 = ax2.bar(x - width/2, memories, width, label='Memory (GB)', color='#A23B72')
ax2.set_ylabel('Memory (GB)', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_title('Memory Usage', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xticks(x)
ax2.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=15, ha='right')
ax2.legend()
ax2.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars2:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax2.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height,
             f'{int(height)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

plt.suptitle('LLM Performance Comparison at Same Batch Size', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('llm_comparison_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
print("Chart saved as llm_comparison_chart.png")
plt.close()"}

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('llm_metrics.json', 'r') as f:

function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

function.name: write

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: grep

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

function.name: find

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

function.name: ls
function.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)
